prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, and for its first experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: After the full exchange my preferred configuration is unchanged: B008 as a single part to Kane, Mele and Molenkamp. The scientific core is a simple and general mechanism. In a time-reversal-invariant insulator with spin-orbit coupling the band structure carries a Z2 invariant, and a nonzero value forces protected helical edge states. Kane and Mele wrote this down in a minimal model and showed that it defines a class of matter distinct from the integer quantum Hall state. Molenkamp's group then observed the quantised edge conductance in HgTe/CdTe wells. The idea was later confirmed independently in three dimensions by ARPES and STM and transferred to photonics, acoustics and cold atoms, so it is mature and understood, not only observed. The round-1 exchange sharpened my view in two ways. First, Eriksson's distinction holds up: the 2016 prize covered topological phase transitions and the integer quantum Hall lineage (Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless, Thouless-Haldane), whereas the Z2 classification with spin-orbit coupling and time-reversal symmetry is a separate discovery. Second, the chair's observation that the real question is whether the attribution objection to B008 and the novelty objection to B035 are decisive helps me. I do not think either is decisive. The attribution objection is real but bounded: the citation can be anchored on the prediction of the state and its first observation, where Kane, Mele and Molenkamp are the clear core, and the committee has accepted a three-name limit before while crediting the conceptual origin and the decisive experiment. B008 also has the broadest opening support, with six of eight members in their top three and the same trio proposed by all six.
statement.case_against: The attribution gap is the main weakness and I do not claim it is closed. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicted the HgTe system that Molenkamp measured, and Johansson, Olsson, Pearce and Kroll are right that a prize crediting the measurement without the proposal that told the experimentalists where to look is uncomfortable. Zhang's death in 2018 removes one claimant but not the question, and Bernevig and Hughes are living. The three-person limit means the 3D generalisation (Fu-Kane-Mele, Moore-Balents, Roy) and Hasan's ARPES are also left out. Against that, Kane and Mele's Z2 insight is the conceptual origin and BHZ is the materials-specific step, which is a real but secondary role. The 2016 prize remains the nearest precedent for B008, and a committee that applies a strict adjacency standard to circuit QED after 2025 must be prepared to apply a comparable one here. I think it passes, because the subject is a different state of matter and not a continuation of the same discovery, but this is a judgement, not a proof. Practical applications are still limited and edge transport in real devices is subtler than the clean picture, so the case rests on the physics.

responses.point: Kroll recognises B008 as the strongest alternative, asks the condensed-matter members how decisive the BHZ proposal was for Molenkamp's experiment, and prefers B035 because its attribution chain from proposal to demonstration is shorter.
responses.response: I will answer his question directly. BHZ was decisive for the choice of HgTe and for the predicted critical thickness, which is why Molenkamp's group could design the experiment so quickly. It was not the discovery of the effect. The Z2 invariant, the helical edge states and the protection against backscattering were in Kane and Mele's 2005 papers, and Bernevig and Zhang had written a different proposal before that. So the credit is layered, not contested, and I would rank the BHZ role as materials prediction within an established concept. I accept that the lattice clock has a shorter chain of credit, but a shorter chain is not the same as a deeper discovery. If the committee wants to be fully safe on attribution it will have to accept a more modest prize, and I do not think that a cleaner attribution alone is sufficient reason to prefer the clock.

responses.point: Lindroth argues that the lattice clock is a new physical idea, the magic wavelength, that combines many-atom statistics with freedom from motional shifts, and not a refinement of the ion clock; she says she could support B008 but does not find it cleaner on credit.
responses.response: I find her argument for the lattice concept more persuasive after round 1 than when I wrote my first statement, and I withdraw the suggestion that B035 is a mere extension of the 2005 and 2012 prizes. Katori's idea changes the physics of how a clock is built. Where we still differ is the standard of surprise, which she herself says she normally applies to favour discoveries about nature. On that standard a new state of matter with a topological invariant and protected edge channels is a more fundamental finding than a better clock. I also agree that her point about atomic-structure theory is a strength of B035, since the systematic corrections are calculable. On credit I concede that B035 is cleaner, but I would not call B008 unsound: its core is three names, and the omission is of a materials prediction, not of the concept.

responses.point: Pearce, as chair, now prefers B035, calls B008 a conceptual advance and his first alternative, and objects that crediting Molenkamp's measurement while leaving out the proposal he tested is the kind of attribution to avoid.
responses.response: I take that objection seriously and I think the right answer is in the citation wording. If the citation credits the prediction of the Z2 quantum spin Hall state and its first experimental realisation, then it credits Kane and Mele for the prediction and Molenkamp for the realisation, and it does not claim that Molenkamp tested Kane and Mele's own material proposal. Graphene was Kane and Mele's example, and it was not the system in which the effect was seen. This is not a perfect solution, and I accept that BHZ will feel overlooked. On the chair's request that we apply one standard of adjacency to B008 and B035, my answer is that both pass: 2016 covered a different discovery from Z2, and 2005 and 2012 covered tools different from the lattice clock. If so, adjacency does not separate them, and the committee has to choose on depth of discovery and attribution, which are the points on which we disagree.

responses.point: Johansson holds that BHZ made the specific prediction that told Molenkamp where to look, that the 2016 prize is a closer precedent than Eriksson acknowledges, and that B004 needs a gap after 2025.
responses.response: I agree with him on B004 and I have dropped it from my alternatives in favour of B023, because a gap after 2025 and the missing Girvin credit are real. On the 2016 precedent I disagree in degree. The 2016 citation named topological phase transitions and topological phases of matter, and the work honoured was the integer quantum Hall classification and the Haldane chain and model. Kane and Mele's work uses time-reversal symmetry and strong spin-orbit coupling, and the Z2 invariant does not exist without them, so it is not a corollary of Thouless-Haldane. I accept that a committee could still see the field as already honoured, and I list that as a genuine uncertainty. On BHZ I accept his statement of the facts and answer it with the same point I made to Kroll, that the specific material prediction is a secondary role.

responses.point: Danielsson prefers B023 on the standard that IceCube found something nature had not told us before, and says B008 is a strong candidate whose trio is contested.
responses.response: I share the standard. A flux of astrophysical PeV neutrinos is a clue from nature, and so is a protected helical edge state in a bulk insulator, which no one expected to be quantised until the Z2 argument. Where I part company is attribution: he concedes that Karle, AMANDA and DUMAND cannot be separated from a collaboration of hundreds, and he would want that said openly. That is a heavier problem than the BHZ omission, because there the core concept is clearly in three names. I would keep B023 as my second alternative because the diffuse flux is established and the committee would be able to cite the detector and the flux, but I would want an expert report on the AMANDA lineage first.

responses.point: Olsson would support B008 if condensed-matter colleagues can show the HgTe experiment is rightly credited to the Kane-Mele proposal alone, and says she cannot call the credit clean while the BHZ prediction sits outside the three names.
responses.response: I do not claim the HgTe experiment follows from the Kane-Mele proposal alone, and the citation should not say so. My claim is narrower: the state, its invariant and its helical edge channels originate with Kane and Mele, and the first observation of that state is Molenkamp's. BHZ identified where it could be seen, and the committee can state this openly in its background material without changing the three names. I would also point out that the three-person limit forces a choice on every shortlisted topic, as Karle and Spiering show in B023 and Lemonde and Boyd in B035. I would apply the same test to all of them: is the core concept and its first realisation in the three names. For B008 and B035 I think it is.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts that the BHZ materials prediction is a secondary role that can be left out of the citation, or regards it as disqualifying; I do not think it disqualifying but I cannot prove it.
Whether the 2016 prize is regarded as covering too much of the same ground, and whether the committee applies the same adjacency standard to B008 and B035.

Whether the committee prefers B035 for its shorter attribution chain and calculable systematics over B008 for conceptual novelty; this is the real difference between the two leading positions and I could be persuaded to support B035 if the committee judges attribution to be decisive.
Whether a B008 plus B035 pairing would be useful; it would exceed the three-person limit (five names), so I do not propose it.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict or recusal to report. None of Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Katori, Ye or the other credited candidates is a known co-author, collaborator or institutional colleague. I note that Johansson and Olsson are in the Gothenburg physics environment (Chalmers) and that Johansson has disclosed his own ties to B004. My field is stochastic and complex-systems physics, not condensed-matter topology or atomic metrology, so my judgement rests on the conceptual argument and I defer to colleagues on experimental details.
